cohort: The study included 38 singleton pregnancies with idiopathic polyhydramnios as cases and 65 singleton pregnancies without polyhydramnios as controls.
finding: Idiopathic polyhydramnios is associated with increased risks of preterm delivery, neonatal distress, and maternal hemorrhage, as well as lower Apgar scores and higher rates of LGA newborns and NICU admission.
mod_finding: Idiopathic polyhydramnios is associated with a significantly higher prevalence of cesarean section delivery (76.3% vs. 23.1%).
